en.name: Anastasius II
en.summary: A pope whose conciliatory approach toward Constantinople over the Acacian Schism provoked suspicion and division within the Roman clergy.
en.body: Anastasius II attempted to ease the ongoing Acacian Schism by communicating more openly with Constantinople and reportedly accepting the validity of Acacius's earlier ordinations, a stance some contemporaries viewed as dangerously conciliatory. His sudden death amid this controversy was later, unreliably, portrayed by some medieval writers as a divine judgment, and it was followed by a contested double election between Symmachus and Laurentius.
